output.brief: Cancelling RotaWeave is unlikely to fix this. The loss is concentrated at Dock Street and Westgate, which have both the app and no coordinator. Millbrook has the app and a coordinator and is nearly flat. Quarry Lane has no coordinator and no app, and it is also nearly flat. So neither change alone explains the drop. Together they do. The app's basic tier only releases open shifts on Thursdays, and nobody now books regulars into their usual slots. Before 1 May staff made about 74 such bookings a week at these two sites. Since then they make about 3. Of 213 regulars there, 129 lost their usual slot at least twice, and 88% of them are now inactive. Only 11% of those who kept their slot are inactive. Background checks and Commonplate do not explain it. 121 of the 123 who lapsed held a current check, and only 2 of 61 callbacks mentioned another group. Low satisfaction looks like a symptom. Next steps: put an admin seat to use at Dock Street and Westgate, and have someone book regulars into their usual slots before each Thursday release. Phone lapsed regulars to offer their slot back, and review after 60 days. Don't cancel the contract, suspend checks, or purge the roster. Confidence is fairly high. The main gaps are that the slot-loss link rests on one manager's reconciliation and that callbacks reached only 61 people.
